final_prompt:
I want a personal habit tracker running today, so the goal is the thinnest working version, not a polished one. It's for one user on one machine, with no login. Throwaway structure is fine, so don't build abstractions. Don't write tests.

Stack: a web app that runs locally in the browser, written in TypeScript. Store all data in the browser's localStorage, with no server and no database. Pick the simplest TypeScript setup that runs locally and that you can scaffold in one session, and say in your summary what you chose and why.

Build only these features:
- [ ] Add a habit and delete a habit.
- [ ] Track multiple habits at once.
- [ ] Check off each habit for today.
- [ ] Show a streak counter for each habit.
- [ ] Show a simple 30-day history for each habit. It is not a weekly or monthly view.

Look and feel: dark mode by default.

Out of scope: reminders and charts. Do not build them.

Work in a new folder and pick a sensible name for it. Don't touch anything outside it.

Verify by running the app locally. Run the type-check and build, and fix the root cause of any errors. Then open the app in the browser and click through this flow:
1. Add a habit.
2. Check it off for today.
3. See the streak and the 30-day history.
4. Reload the page and confirm the data persists.
If any of these steps can't run, report that instead of claiming it works.

Carry the whole checklist through without pausing. Ask me only if you are blocked. For details I didn't specify (names, styling, how a streak handles a missed day), decide and note your choice in the summary.

You're done when the checklist above is built, the type-check and build pass, and the click-through flow works in the browser. Then stop. Put any extra ideas in your summary and don't build them. Give the summary the folder path and the command to start the app.
